subject: Message Empty reply from server while Loading JDBC driver

messages.author: faa5427c06a1e034
messages.subject: Message Empty reply from server while Loading JDBC driver
parts:
Hi,

I am getting a message 'Empty reply from server'  -  while Loading JDBC driver

Code:

[root@localhost R]# cat hello.R
library("plyr")
library("ggplot2")
library("reshape")
library("scales")
require("scales")
library("RJDBC")
JDBC("com.mysql.jdbc.Driver", "/usr/share/java/mysql-connector-java.jar", identifier.quote="`")
print("Printing data...")
[root@localhost R]#


Response:

[perf@localhost src]$ curl http://localhost/rapachetest
curl: (52) Empty reply from server
[perf@localhost src]$


Apache Logs

[root@localhost logs]# pwd
/etc/httpd/logs
[root@localhost logs]# tail -f *_log
[Fri Jul 06 17:07:22 2012] [error] [client 127.0.0.1] rApache Notice!

I have tested this code using R terminal and it works well. Could you please help?

Regards
Santosh

messages.subject: Re: Message Empty reply from server while Loading JDBC driver
parts: The problem is that RApache is closing the connection/ breaking when the following line of code is executed.
JDBC("com.mysql.jdbc.Driver", "/usr/share/java/mysql-connector-java.jar", identifier.quote="`")

I followed your hello world video and modified my code as shown below.

hello world...
<% print(rnorm(10)); %>
<%

library("plyr")
library("ggplot2")
library("reshape")
library("scales")
require("scales")
library("RJDBC")

library("brew")
%>

<%
loadjdbcdriver <- function() {

JDBC("com.mysql.jdbc.Driver", "/usr/share/java/mysql-connector-java.jar", identifier.quote="`")
}

printError <- function(e) {
  print(e$message);
}
tryCatch(loadjdbcdriver(), error=printError);
%>

When I execute this code, I get a message in the browser:

No data received

Unable to load the web page because the server sent no data.

Error 324 (net::ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE): The server closed the connection without sending any data. 

Apache log does not show any error message apart from rApache Notice! but this messages appears even when the line/fucntion to load JDBC driver is commented.

==> access_log <==
xx.xx.xx.xx - - [09/Jul/2012:10:36:18 +0100] "GET /brew/test.R HTTP/1.1" 200 141 "-" "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; rv:11.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/11.0"
==> error_log <==
[Mon Jul 09 10:37:17 2012] [error] [client  xx.xx.xx.xx ] rApache Notice!

If I comment the line tryCatch(loadjdbcdriver(), error=printError); it works and gives the following output.

hello world...

 [1]  0.2046978 -1.5312598  0.8392630 -0.1469732  0.7051654  0.7554666
 [7] -1.7833873 -0.7203613  0.4877860 -1.3196503

I am struggling to understand the reason why RApache is breaking when I load JDBC driver.

The code works when executed through R terminal (see below)

> library("plyr")
> library("ggplot2")
> library("reshape")

Attaching package: \u2018reshape\u2019

The following object(s) are masked from \u2018package:plyr\u2019:

    rename, round_any

> library("scales")
> require("scales")
> library("RJDBC")

Loading required package: DBI
Loading required package: rJava
Warning message:
replacing previous import \u2018show\u2019 when loading \u2018rJava\u2019 
> library("brew")
> loadjdbcdriver <- function() {
+    JDBC("com.mysql.jdbc.Driver", "/usr/share/java/mysql-connector-java.jar", identifier.quote="`")
+ ;
+ ;
+ }
> loadjdbcdriver <- function() {
+    JDBC("com.mysql.jdbc.Driver", "/usr/share/java/mysql-connector-java.jar", identifier.quote="`")
+ }
> printError <- function(e) {
+   print(e$message);
+ }
> tryCatch(loadjdbcdriver(), error=printError);
An object of class "JDBCDriver"
Slot "identifier.quote":
[1] "`"

Slot "jdrv":
[1] "Java-Object{com.mysql.jdbc.Driver@7d2152e6}"

>

Could you please help?

Regards
Santosh

messages.subject: Re: Message Empty reply from server while Loading JDBC driver
parts:
I included LD_LIBRARY_PATH and PATH settings @ apache startup. Restarted apache.

RApache now loads the JDBC driver successfully. After the JDBC driver is loaded, when I try to connect to the database using the following code, I get error message in apache.

conn <- dbConnect(jdbcdriver, "jdbc:mysql://<hostname-removed>/test", "root", "<password-removed>")

The error message is:

==> error_log <==
[Wed Jul 11 17:31:15 2012] [error] [client <ip-removed>] rApache Notice!
Error in .jcall(drv@jdrv, "Ljava/sql/Connection;", "connect", as.character(url)[1],  : 
  com.mysql.jdbc.exceptions.jdbc4.CommunicationsException: Communications link failure

The last packet sent successfully to the server was 0 milliseconds ago. The driver has not received any packets from the server.
Traceback:
9: stop(list(message = "com.mysql.jdbc.exceptions.jdbc4.CommunicationsException: Communications link failure\n\nThe last packet sent successfully to the server was 0 milliseconds ago. The driver has not received any packets from the server.", 
       call = .jcall(drv@jdrv, "Ljava/sql/Connection;", "connect", 
           as.character(url)[1], p), jobj = <S4 object of class "jobjRef">))
8: .Call(RJavaCheckExceptions, silent)
7: .jcheck(silent = FALSE)
6: .jcall(drv@jdrv, "Ljava/sql/Connection;", "connect", as.character(url)[1], 
       p)
5: .local(drv, ...)
4: is(object, Cl)
3: is(object, Cl)
2: .valueClassTest(standardGeneric("dbConnect"), "DBIConnection", 
       "dbConnect")
1: dbConnect(jdbcdriver, "jdbc:mysql://<hostname-removed>/test", "root", 
       "<password-removed>")

The code (below) works on R terminal:

library("RJDBC")
#print ("Hello...JDBC")
#
jdbcdriver <- JDBC("com.mysql.jdbc.Driver", "/usr/share/java/mysql-connector-java.jar", identifier.quote="`")
conn <- dbConnect(jdbcdriver, "jdbc:mysql://<host-name-removed>/test", "root", "<password-removed>")

Regards
Santosh

On Wednesday, July 11, 2012 2:24:22 PM UTC+1, SantoshMarigowda wrote:
How do I do this?

I think I may need to use REvalOnStartup/ RSourceOnStartup, please advise.

Regards
Santosh

On Wednesday, July 11, 2012 2:18:40 PM UTC+1, Jeffrey Horner wrote:

You have to set LD_LIBRARY_PATH before you start Apache for it to take effect.

Jeff

and see if there is a difference in your java environment variables.

Jeff
